36/S0.subgoal: Explain what contextual inquiry is, its active and passive modes, and why the observer must act as an apprentice rather than a teacher.

36/S1.subgoal: Describe the five stages of contextual inquiry and how the reflect stage uses affinity diagrams to analyze observed data.

36/S2.subgoal: Explain how the affinity diagram method organizes contextual inquiry notes into grouped design recommendations, using a note-taking application example, and distinguish those recommendations from implementation.

36/S3.subgoal: Demonstrate how affinity diagram grouping can be applied to calendar app observations to form reminder and scheduling requirement categories.

36/S4.subgoal: Summarize the lecture's coverage of contextual inquiry and affinity diagram analysis, and preview the next part on using the data for implementation.

goal.goal: Explain how contextual inquiry and affinity diagram analysis support usability requirement gathering and specification, from observing users to deriving requirement categories and design recommendations.
goal.achieves: It provides the learner with a foundational user-centered method for identifying and specifying usability requirements in an XR system, supporting the later case-study design and implementation stages.

objectives.goal: Explain how contextual inquiry gathers usability requirements through active and passive observation, the master-apprentice observer role, and the plan, initiate, execute, close, and reflect stages.
objectives.achieves: It lets the learner plan and carry out user observation in an XR task domain to identify the usability issues and design goals that will inform a requirement specification.

objectives.goal: Use the affinity diagram method to organize contextual inquiry notes and application observations into grouped design recommendations and requirement categories while distinguishing those recommendations from implementation choices.
objectives.achieves: It lets the learner convert observed user needs in XR applications into concrete usability requirement specifications that can guide later system design and implementation.
